title: Microtrace replay harness design and observability notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a proposed design for a microtrace replay harness and companion observability conventions to help reproduce performance regressions that show up in CI or in customer traces. The goal is deterministic replay + adjustable noise (arrival jitter, concurrency) so we can: 1) reproduce tail-latency regression, 2) validate kernel changes, 3) exercise KV cache cold/warm transitions, 4) quantify scheduler impacts.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: op-level trace format, lightweight recorder, replay engine (local/gpu), kernel sampling hooks, golden-suite definitions, regression detection heuristics, and experiment playbooks.
- Non-goals: full fidelity of system-level scheduling (we won’t model I/O subsystems precisely), full network replay (we will simulate arrivals).

High level design:
1) Trace recorder: embed an efficient op-level tracer in the runtime that emits a compact line-oriented event stream: timestamp, request_id, op_type, kernel_id_hint, seq_len, kv_state_marker (COLD/WARM), batch_id, cpu_ts, gpu_ts(optional). Prefer newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) for simplicity.
2) Canonical trace format: maintain a small schema version field at top of file; include model version and tokenizer seed so tokenization is deterministic. Small payloads only: no raw tokens; use hashes for payload fingerprinting.
3) Replay engine: orchestrates synthetic arrivals derived from recorded arrival timestamps but supports: (a) speedup/slowdown factor, (b) arrival jitter generator, (c) fan-in concurrency multiplier, (d) signal to toggle KV cache state transitions (force cold starts).
4) Microbench harness: can run op-level microbench for a single kernel with deterministic inputs and capture nvtx/CUPTI counters. This is separate but integrated to seed kernel latency priors.

KV cache handling:
- Explicit markers in trace: on request boundary events mark whether the KV cache state was observed to be COLD/WARM.
- Replay semantics: when encountering COLD marker, the replay engine flushes simulated KV state for that request path so runtime takes cold-path code (and measures associated kernel invocations). We also support toggling partial warm (e.g., simulate half-warm by preloading some layers’ caches).

Scheduling simulation and batching:
- Two modes: deterministic batcher (replay arrival ordering exactly) and probabilistic batcher (respect target batching policy but inject jitter).
- Provide knobs for batching policy: max_batch_size, max_latency_ms, and priority preemption. Use these to stress test changes to the scheduler.

Kernel sampling and instrumentation:
- Kernel selection hints from trace are used to quickly find candidate kernels to instrument.
- Attach lightweight sampling: per-op wallclock, per-op GPU time from CUDA events, and optional CUPTI counters for SM utilization and memory throughput.
- For high-signal debugging, a capture mode will emit full nvprof-style timelines for a single request.

Regression detection heuristics (CI integration):
- Golden trace suite: small curated set (~20) of traces representing common and taily workloads (short chat, long-form generation, beam use-cases, embedding bursts). Each trace has expected distributions (p50/p90/p99 of token latency, token throughput, memory sys usage).
- Statistical checks: compare current run to baseline using a combo of EWMA for p50 drift and KS-test for distributional shift for p90/p99. Also check deterministic invariants (op counts, kernel invocation sequence).
- Alert rules: fail CI if p99 increases > 15% and KS p-value < 0.01 OR if op sequence diverges. For less severe drift, create a perf incident with attached replay artifacts.

Telemetry and observability conventions:
- Use NDJSON fields: trace_id, request_shard, model_tag, runtime_git_sha, hw_profile. Include a small fingerprint to locate matching CI run.
- Standard metrics emitted after replay run: token_latency_histogram (hdr), kernel_latency_table (CSV), kv_cache_miss_rate, batch_size_histogram, gpu_sm_utilization_avg.
- All artifacts (trace, summarized metrics, nvtx zip) go into a reproducible s3 path: s3://perf-replays/{date}/{trace_name}/{run_id}/

Experiment plan (short-term):
1) Implement minimal recorder (ndjson) and one offline parser -> 2 weeks.
2) Implement a local replay engine (cpu-based control loop, cuda kernels executed on GPU) -> 3 weeks.
3) Add microbench harness and CUPTI toggles -> 2 weeks.
4) Curate golden traces and CI integration (baseline storage, comparison infra) -> 2 weeks.

Longer-term ideas:
- Cross-machine trace stitching to reproduce multi-host scheduling issues.
- Fuzzed arrival generator that mutates token lengths and arrival jitter to hunt brittle scheduler assumptions.
- Model-aware prefill strategies to simulate partial-kv warm starts realistically.

Playbook for debugging a regression using the harness:
1) Run CI golden replay that failed and upload artifacts.
2) Locally replay the failing trace with deterministic timing.
3) Enable full nvtx capture for single-request failure reproduction.
4) If kernel latencies match baseline but latency still regressed, toggled scheduler knobs (batch sizes, preemption) to isolate.
5) If op sequence differs, dump kernel selection hint mismatch and check model/tokenizer seed mismatches.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Schema: finalize ndjson schema and versioning strategy (rolling changes).
- Privacy: define PII-safe trace export (hashing tokens is OK, but confirm product/legal).
- Resource isolation: how to run multiple concurrent replays on shared CI GPUs without noise leakage.
- Define a small set of deterministic seeds for tokenizer to avoid tokenization-induced nondeterminism.

Notes and references:
- Related PR: runtime#987 (replay primitives).
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread "replay-harness".
- Confluence: perf/golden-traces (living doc).

Owner: Daniel Park. Please comment on tradeoffs for full fidelity vs. reproducibility and on the CI thresholds for p99 failures.
